battle.name: 隋與突厥達頭可汗之戰
battle.brief: 開皇十九年（599）正月，隋文帝乘突厥內部分裂，發兵三十萬分六路出塞。靈州行軍總管楊素夜襲達頭可汗牙營得手，乘勝追至陰山鐵山，達頭眾潰，餘眾十餘萬降隋。卡面羅馬重步兵不在此役現場，但它那套靠補充兵源與補給線打戰爭的辦法，正是隋軍此刻取勝的憑依。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰雙方是北方的隋朝與草原上的第二突厥汗國，但真正左右戰局的第三股力量，是突厥內部正在互相攻殺的兩位可汗。隋朝這邊，開皇十九年（599）時在位的是隋文帝楊堅，開皇年號已行到第十九年；軍政大權握在楊素、高熲等關隴集團核心手中，兵制以府兵為骨幹，輔以宿衛禁軍、州鎮戍兵，以及各次戰役臨時募發的雜役與驂騎。開皇十八年（598）冬，隋文帝詔發兵三十萬，分六路出塞：並州總管李秀當井陘道攻定襄，幽州總管韋世康自北平道出，靈州總管楊素當靈武道，秦州總管衛叔寶當金城道，齊州總管李藥與潁州方面各當一路；衛王楊廣、齊王楊暕、楚王楊諒、代王楊慶並行，以行軍元帥王誼總節度，楊素為元帥長史。靈州是全軍樞紐：它控制黃河上游與河西走廊東口，向北可援朔州，向西可達涼州與西域商路，隋軍的糧道、軍馬徵集與降戶安置都以這裡為中心。突厥那邊，達頭可汗阿史那·莫葛是頉利可汗阿史那·咄格的弟弟，名義上與兄長分掌草原，他這一支部眾聚居在漠北西部與河西以北的沙陀、薛延陀一帶，以牙帳為中樞，諸部散牧，沒有固定城郭，靠逐水草而居的騎兵與分散的部落組織維持戰力；編制上分為可汗直屬的近衛騎、各部貝勒的部眾與臨時徵發的丁騎，重騎與輕騎混編，傾巢出動時可達二十萬騎上下的規模。真正令隋朝敢於深入草原的，是突厥東西兩部的分裂：達頭與頉利互相攻伐，隋朝只要讓兩邊繼續打下去，就能用邊塞的小股兵力牽制草原主力。
countriesEn: The two parties in this war were the Sui dynasty in the north and the Second Turkic Khaganate on the steppe, though a third force really decided the outcome: the two khans who were busy destroying each other inside the Turkic camp. On the Sui side, Emperor Wen, Yang Jian, had ruled since 581 and the Kaihuang era had already reached its nineteenth year. Military authority rested with the core of the Guanlong group, Yang Su and Gao Zhi among them. The army was built on the fubing militia, backed by the palace guard, the garrison troops of the prefectures and commanderies, and the miscellaneous levies and auxiliaries mustered for each campaign. In the winter of 598, the eighteenth year of Kaihuang, the emperor ordered three hundred thousand men into the field and split them into six columns: Li Xiu, zongguan of Bingzhou, took the Jingxing route against Dingxiang; Wei Shikang, zongguan of Youzhou, marched out along the Beiping route; Yang Su, zongguan of Lingzhou, held the Lingwu route; Wei Shubao, zongguan of Qinzhou, took the Jincheng route; Li Yao of Qizhou and the men from Yingzhou took one route each. Five princes marched in parallel, with Wang Yi as xingjun yuanshuai holding overall command and Yang Su as his zhangshi. Lingzhou was the hinge of the whole army: it commanded the upper Yellow River and the eastern mouth of the Hexi Corridor, could reinforce Shuozhou to the north, and reached Liangzhou and the western trade roads beyond; the Sui supply line, the drawing of warhorses and the settlement of surrendered households all ran through it. On the Turkic side, Datou Qaghan, Ashina Moge, was the younger brother of Jieli Qaghan, Ashina Duge, and nominally shared the steppe with him. His following was concentrated in the west of the northern steppe and north of the Hexi, among the Shatuo and Xueyantuo, with the qaghan's camp at its centre. There were no fixed cities; the tribes grazed and moved with the water and grass, and the fighting power of the host rested on mounted bands and a loose tribal organisation. It was divided into the qaghan's own guard cavalry, the contingents of the various beiles, and levies raised for the occasion, heavy and light riders mixed, and when the host moved in full it could bring something like two hundred thousand horsemen onto the field. What really allowed the Sui to strike deep into the steppe was the split inside the Turkic state: Datou and Jieli were at war with each other, and the Sui only had to keep the two sides fighting in order to pin the main Turkic strength with small forces along the frontier.
people: 決策核心在長安，親臨前線的是楊素。隋文帝楊堅在開皇十九年已六十餘歲，他不親征，只發詔、調兵、議糧，跨越數千里的戰役全部交給行軍元帥王誼與元帥長史楊素；楊素自太原起家，久鎮西邊，歷北周與隋的西北戰線，開皇十八年冬率軍抵靈州時，面對達頭可汗傾力來犯的二十萬騎，他不硬碰，而是據險固守、待其疲敝，隨後以夜襲破敵。副手方面，並州總管李秀所部在定襄方向受挫，損失慘重，敗還後受到免職的處分，反而逼出主力西進、靈州集中的部署；幽州總管韋世康、秦州總管衛叔寶各當一路，負責牽制與追擊。真正改變戰局走向的是兵部尚書高熲與長孫晟一系的謀劃：高熲主張用離間把達頭與頉利之間的裂痕拉得更深，長孫晟早在開皇初年就已證明，可以用少量使節與詐謀讓草原諸部自相攻伐；高熲又設計讓頉利可汗的兒子啟民可汗安居隋境，一旦需要便令其內應，使頉利腹背受敵。突厥那邊，達頭可汗莫葛的死並非全由隋軍造成：據《隋書·突厥傳》，達頭與兄長頉利交攻，部眾怨恨其殘暴，開皇十九年達頭被部下所殺，死前單騎出走，眾皆散潰；其子意珍保收拾餘眾自立，是為登利可汗，後來在仁壽元年（601）被隋軍擒斬，東突厥汗國至此崩解。另一端的內應者啟民可汗，則在隋朝保護下成為漠南新的統治者，隋亡之後仍以啟民可汗的名號見於史冊。
peopleEn: The decisions were made at Chang'an, but the fighting was led by Yang Su. Emperor Wen was over sixty by the nineteenth year of Kaihuang; he never took the field himself, only issuing orders, shifting troops and discussing grain, and he left an expedition of several thousand li entirely in the hands of the xingjun yuanshuai Wang Yi and his zhangshi Yang Su. Yang Su, a native of Taiyuan, had long served on the western frontier under Northern Zhou and Sui. When he reached Lingzhou in the winter of 598 he faced the full host of some two hundred thousand horsemen that Datou Qaghan brought against him. He refused to meet them head on, held a strong position, waited for the enemy to tire, and only then broke them with a night attack. Among his subordinates, the force of Li Xiu, zongguan of Bingzhou, was checked in the Dingxiang direction with heavy losses; Li Xiu was dismissed after the defeat, and it was that reverse which pushed the Sui to concentrate its main effort westward at Lingzhou. Wei Shikang of Youzhou and Wei Shubao of Qinzhou each took a route of their own, charged with containing the enemy and pursuing defeated men. What really bent the course of the war was the planning of Gao Zhi, zhangbu shangshu, and of the school around Changsun Sheng: Gao Zhi argued for widening the rift between Datou and Jieli, and Changsun Sheng had already shown as early as the first years of Kaihuang that a few envoys and a handful of false promises could set the steppe tribes fighting among themselves. Gao Zhi also arranged for Jieli's son, Qimin Qaghan, to live inside Sui territory, so that he could be used as an internal agent and Jieli could be attacked from within while under pressure outside. On the Turkic side, Datou's death was not caused by Sui steel alone. According to the Biography of the Turks in the Book of Sui, Datou and his elder brother Jieli were at war, his followers resented his cruelty, and in 599 Datou was killed by his own men; before his death he rode out alone and the host scattered. His son Yizhenbao gathered the remnants and took the title of Dengli Qaghan; he was captured and beheaded by Sui forces in 601, the first year of Renshou, and the Eastern Turkic state came apart with him. The other man of the piece, Qimin Qaghan, became the new ruler of the southern steppe under Sui protection, and after the fall of the Sui his name still appears in the histories.
kits: 卡面上這件兵器是羅馬重步兵（Legionary）：分段式鎖子鎧甲，配大橢圓盾、短劍與投槍，制度成形於公元前一百年前後的羅馬軍營，離開皇十九年的塞外戰場已有六百九十九年。它並不是開皇十九年戰場上的實際裝備，然而這張卡指出的辦法——羅馬的戰力靠補充兵源與補給線，不靠重裝——恰恰是這場戰爭取勝的邏輯。隋軍這邊，重裝步兵是府兵中的甲士：著兩當甲、兜鍪，長柄武器用槊與戟，配大盾或腰盾列陣；遠程火力以弩為主，蹶張弩與床弩在陣前齊射，臂弩隨騎兵攜行；陣前布拒馬槊與拒鹿角一類的障礙器材，據《通典》記載是隋代所制、唐代沿用，用來擋住突厥騎兵的衝鋒。馬匹是真正的瓶頸：隋軍的戰馬多來自河西與西域的良馬，經涼州、甘肅一帶的馬市交易取得，隨軍另備替馬，否則千里追擊撐不住。糧食以粟為主，配麥、豆、鹽、醋，乾餅與肉脯隨軍；牛車拖著糧車走，帳幕用氈張，士卒自攜十日之糧，這支部隊才能離開城塞作縱深作戰。突厥騎兵的裝備則是另一套：皮甲或鑲骨甲，多不配重甲，角弓與筋弓射速快，骨鏃與鐵鏃兼用，配修長標槍與短刀，馬上高鞍利於拈弓，紀律散漫但耐力驚人，能連續奔馳數日不食。兩套體系接觸的地方就在正面：隋軍以方陣、大盾與長槊硬扛騎兵衝鋒，靠弩的齊射把衝鋒打散，再以兩翼騎兵反擊側後。對照羅馬重步兵的分段鎧甲與重盾，隋軍甲士的防具在工藝上更輕，卻同樣是一種「把正面變成一堵牆」的辦法；而兩者真正相同的地方都在背後——羅馬靠後備兵源與從行省輸送的糧食養活前線，隋朝靠均田農民提供的兵源與漕運、屯田維持的糧道。戰後達頭部眾十餘萬降隋，編入州郡與屯田，正是把「補充兵源」這一步做到底。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is a Roman legionary: segmentary lorica segmentata, a large oval scutum, a short sword and a throwing spear, an institution that took shape in the Roman army around 100 BC, six hundred and ninety-nine years before the field outside the Great Wall in the nineteenth year of Kaihuang. It was not the actual equipment of Kaihuang 19, and yet the card names the principle that actually won this war: Roman strength rested on replenishing manpower and on the supply line, not on armour. On the Sui side the heavy infantry were the armoured men of the fubing: a two-piece lamellar cuirass and a helmet, long spears and halberds, a large shield or a waist shield carried in front. Long-range fire came from the crossbows, the juzhang nu and the bed crossbow for massed shots in front of the line, the arm bow carried by the cavalry, and the front of the line was studded with juma shuang and julu jiao, obstacle devices that according to the Tongdian were a Sui invention kept by the Tang, planted to stop Turkic horsemen from breaking through. Horses were the real bottleneck: most of the Sui warhorses were the fine animals of the Hexi and the western regions, bought through the horse markets of Liangzhou and Ganzhou, with remounts carried along, because a pursuit of a thousand li could not be sustained otherwise. The food was chiefly millet, with wheat, beans, salt and vinegar, dried cakes and dried meat travelling with the troops; ox-drawn carts dragged the grain wagons, tents were made of felt, and each man carried ten days' rations, which was what allowed this host to leave the walled towns and operate deep in the steppe. The Turkic horseman was equipped along quite another line: leather or bone-studded armour, usually without heavy protection, bows of horn and sinew with a fast draw, bone and iron arrowheads used together, long lances and short knives, and a high saddle that made the bow easier to handle; discipline was loose but endurance remarkable, for the riders could gallop for days without eating. The two systems met at the point of contact: the Sui met the charge with a square, shields and long spears, broke the charge with massed crossbow fire, and sent their own cavalry around the flanks. Set beside the Roman legionary's segmentata and heavy shield, the Sui armoured infantry were technically lighter but served the same purpose, turning the front of the line into a wall, and the deeper truth was the same on both sides: Rome fed its front line with replacement troops and with grain from the provinces, and the Sui fed theirs with the manpower of the equal-field peasantry and with grain moved by river transport and by the military farms on the frontier. The more than a hundred thousand who surrendered after Datou's death were enrolled in the prefectures and in the farms, which was the replenishment of manpower carried to its conclusion.
tactics: 隋軍的戰術核心只有兩條：不要在草原上跟二十萬騎兵硬拼正面，要把他們拖到沒水沒草、沒處可退的樣子。開皇十八年冬，楊素率主力抵靈州，兵力不足以與達頭可汗傾力來犯的二十萬騎相抗，便據險而營，閉門不戰，蓄銳待疲；達頭屢次挑戰不得，遂解營而稍懈，隋軍這才以夜襲掩襲其連營，斬獲數千級，達頭眾遂奔潰，隋軍乘勝追擊，迫其不能重新結集。開皇十九年正月，五路大軍齊進：井陘道、幽州道、靈武道、金城道、齊州與潁州方向同時壓上，把草原的縱深切成數段；李秀一路攻定襄受挫，敗還後被免職，其餘各路則以正面壓制配合靈州一路的深入。追擊是這場戰爭最吃力的部分：隋軍自靈州向北追過黃河，遠達鐵山、磧口一線，全程約四百至五百公里，穿越的是沒有城鎮、只有草場的河套與陰山南麓；塞外正月、二月仍嚴寒多風，草原尚未返青，馬匹草料與飲水都要靠隨軍輸送解決，因此隋軍要靠沿途的屯田糧倉與分遣的驛騎維持，另以輕騎分隊以戰養戰。防守與掩護方面，步兵結方陣，大盾拒馬列於陣前，槊手斜舉長槊迎擊騎兵，弩手在陣後分層齊射，騎兵於兩翼展開，尋找突厥騎隊的側後；輜重車隊居中，牛車與護騎夾護糧車，一旦前方失利，糧車是必須先保住的東西。更高的一層是外交與離間：高熲與長孫晟一系用使節往來、贈馬賜旗、散布部族互相猜忌，把達頭與頉利的內戰推到失控，再安排啟民可汗在頉利軍中內應，使隋軍不必獨力承擔全部草原兵力。達頭正是在這樣的內外夾擊下崩潰：開皇十九年他被自己的部下所殺，眾遂大潰，單騎遁走，餘眾十餘萬降隋。
tacticsEn: The Sui tactical plan rested on two points: do not meet two hundred thousand horsemen head on in the open steppe, but drag them until they have no water, no grass and nowhere to retreat. In the winter of 598 Yang Su brought the main body to Lingzhou with too few men to stand up to the full host of two hundred thousand horsemen that Datou Qaghan brought against him, so he entrenched on strong ground, kept his lines closed, stored up his strength and waited for the enemy to tire. Datou could not force a battle, so he relaxed his camp, and only then did the Sui strike at night against his chained encampments, taking several thousand by head count and scattering the rest, and they pursued the broken enemy so that he could not reform. In the first month of 599 the six columns advanced together: the Jingxing, Beiping, Lingwu, Jincheng, Qizhou and Yingzhou routes pressed in at once, cutting the depth of the steppe into sections. Li Xiu's column was checked at Dingxiang and came back broken, and he was dismissed; the other columns pressed from the front while the Lingzhou route drove deep. The pursuit was the hardest part of the campaign. The Sui rode north from Lingzhou, crossed the Yellow River and reached as far as the Tieshan and Qikou line, roughly four hundred to five hundred kilometres, through the Hetao and the southern foot of the Yin Mountains where there were no towns, only pasture. In the first and second months of the year the country beyond the wall was still bitterly cold and windy and the grass had not yet come up, so fodder and water for the horses had to travel with the army; the Sui therefore relied on the granaries of the frontier farms and on dispatch riders to keep going, with light cavalry squadrons living off the country as they moved. In defence and cover, the infantry closed into squares, with large shields and juma spears set in front, spearmen holding their long spears at an angle against the charge and crossbowmen firing in layered volleys from the rear, while the cavalry worked the flanks looking for the Turkic horse-lines; the baggage train sat in the middle, ox carts and escort cavalry guarding the grain wagons, because if the front failed, the grain wagons were the things that had to be saved first. Above all of this sat diplomacy and division: Gao Zhi and the men around Changsun Sheng used embassies, gifts of horses and banners, and rumour to set the Turkic tribes against one another and to push the war between Datou and Jieli past breaking point, while Qimin Qaghan was placed inside Jieli's camp as an agent, so that the Sui would not have to face the whole steppe host alone. Datou broke under exactly this pressure from two sides: in 599 he was killed by his own men, the host dissolved, he rode off alone, and more than a hundred thousand of the survivors came over to the Sui.
data: 可以核對的數字大致如下。《資治通鑑》卷一百八十五記開皇十八年十一月，隋文帝「發兵三十萬」擊突厥，分道六路出塞；三十萬是上限，實際投入戰鬥的只是其中一部，其餘是輜重、運輸與隨軍丁夫。《隋書·楊素傳》記達頭可汗率眾二十萬騎來攻靈州，兩軍在靈州、朔州一線反覆周旋，隋軍夜襲得手後斬首數千級，追擊階段的斬獲仍是數千級的規模，並非數十萬。達頭死後「眾十餘萬」降隋，是《隋書·突厥傳》留下的最大的一個數字，也是隋朝此後安置邊外部眾的主要來源。距離上，靈州治所今寧夏靈武，鐵山一般指陰山南麓一線，自靈州至鐵山約四百至五百公里，正好是一支全騎兵大軍三至五日可及、而糧車需要十日以上才能跟上的一段距離，這個速度差是隋軍能追上並拖垮突厥的關鍵。時間上，自開皇十八年冬發兵、十二月楊素抵靈州，到開皇十九年達頭被部下所殺，前後不過三四個月；同年十二月，隋朝詔諸州修築長城，並在塞內外築城置兵、積粟轉運，說明這場戰役的直接結果是改防線而非滅國。兵種比例上，學界一般估計隋唐府兵之中騎兵只佔兩成上下，隋軍的三十萬大軍是以步兵與徵發的雜役為主體、以騎兵為打擊骨幹的混合部隊，這也是為何楊素在靈州必須靠夜襲與突進而非正面對撞。傷亡數字各方記載互相矛盾，此處不列；能確定的只有一點：開皇十九年這場戰爭之後不到三年，隋朝在同一條東突厥戰線上仍打了一場更大規模的戰役，可見這次的勝利並未換來長久的安寧。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked run roughly as follows. The Zizhi Tongjian, volume 185, records that in the eleventh month of Kaihuang 18 the emperor raised three hundred thousand men against the Turks and sent them out in six columns; the three hundred thousand is a ceiling, and only part of it was ever engaged, the rest being baggage, transport and the labouring men who went with the army. The Biography of Yang Su in the Book of Sui records Datou Qaghan coming against Lingzhou with some two hundred thousand horsemen, the two sides working against each other around Lingzhou and Shuozhou, and the Sui night attack ending with several thousand heads taken; the tally of the pursuit is on the same scale, thousands and not tens of thousands. After Datou's death, more than a hundred thousand came over to the Sui, the largest single figure the Book of Sui preserves for this campaign, and the main source of the border population the dynasty later had to settle. In terms of distance, the seat of Lingzhou is modern Lingwu in Ningxia, and Tieshan generally denotes the southern foot of the Yin Mountains; the run from Lingzhou to Tieshan is roughly four hundred to five hundred kilometres, a stretch a fully mounted army could cover in three to five days and that a baggage train needed more than ten to keep up with. That gap in speed is the reason the Sui could catch the Turks and exhaust them. In time, from the mobilisation in the winter of Kaihuang 18 and Yang Su's arrival at Lingzhou in the twelfth month, to Datou's murder by his own men in 599, it was three or four months at most. In the twelfth month of the same year the Sui ordered the prefectures to repair and build the Great Wall, to build forts and station troops both inside and outside the frontier, and to accumulate grain for transport: the campaign's direct outcome was a new line of defence, not the destruction of a state. On the balance of arms, scholarship generally puts mounted fubing at only around a fifth of the total, which means the three hundred thousand was in truth a mass of infantry and conscript labour with cavalry as its striking arm, and it is why Yang Su at Lingzhou had to win by night attack and penetration rather than by a head-on clash. Casualty figures conflict between the sources and are not listed here; what can be said with certainty is that within less than three years of this victory the Sui was fighting a much larger war on the same Eastern Turkic front, which is the surest sign that the win bought no lasting peace.
cause: 打起來的直接原因是達頭可汗犯塞。開皇十八年冬，達頭部眾大舉南下，寇掠太原、朔州、靈州一線的城鎮，掠走人畜與糧秣，把塞內的屯田與邊民拖進戰爭；同一年更早的夏天，隋朝還要分兵救濟關東水旱與山東的飛蝗，兩邊的負擔疊在一起，文帝楊堅不可能再聽任邊警年年響起。深一層的原因是草原政權自身的分裂：頉利可汗坐擁漠北東部與南部大片草場，達頭可汗握有漠北西部與河西以北的部眾，兄弟二人為了汗位與牧地互相攻伐，達頭的部眾同時怨恨其殘暴，隨時可能內變。隋朝看準的正是這個窗口。楊堅在開皇初年已經用長孫晟的離間之策削弱突厥，開皇十八年北邊傳來達頭與頉利交攻的消息，朝廷便決定把打壓突厥提到與滅陳同等的位置，趁突厥內鬥，以六路大軍直取其巢穴。第三個原因是國力已經到得夠。開皇九年（589）高熲括戶，把州郡豪強隱庇的丁口重新登記入籍，國家的租調收入與兵源因此增加；均田、租調與倉庫制度在開皇年間運作順暢，關中、隴右、河西的軍屯與漕運能夠把糧食一路送到靈州，府兵的兵源也因為均田農戶的上升而更為充裕。第四個原因是戰略上的選擇：突厥的騎兵在開闊草原上無敵，一旦被引到河套、朔州之間的狹窄通道與寒冬的草場上，戰力就要打折；隋朝寧可用三十萬人押上來打一場，也不接受突厥年年南下逐鹿中原。第五個原因是外交上的配合：隋朝在開皇十九年把宗女安義公主嫁給頉利可汗，用婚嫁與厚賚拖住漠北主力的注意力，同時把已在隋境內的頉利之子啟民可汗作為內應的棋子留在手裡，使任何一位可汗都不敢在南下時把全部兵力都帶走。
causeEn: The immediate reason for the fighting was Datou Qaghan's raid into the empire. In the winter of 598 his people swept south in strength, raiding the towns along the Taiyuan, Shuozhou and Lingzhou lines, driving off men, livestock and grain and dragging the frontier farms and the border population into the war. Earlier in that same summer the Sui had still been sending relief troops to the floods in the east and the locusts in Shandong, and with the two burdens together Wen di could not afford to let the frontier alarms sound year after year. A deeper cause lay in the split inside the steppe polity itself. Jieli Qaghan held the eastern and southern pastures of the northern steppe, Datou Qaghan the western part and the peoples north of the Hexi; the two brothers fought each other for the khanship and for grazing land, and Datou's own followers resented his cruelty, so that defection was always possible. The Sui had noticed exactly that opening. Yang Jian had already used Changsun Sheng's policy of division to weaken the Turks in the first years of Kaihuang, and in 598 word came from the north that Datou and Jieli were at war, so the court decided to place the campaign against the Turks on the same level as the conquest of Chen and to strike at the heartland of the steppe while the Turks destroyed each other. A third cause was that the state had the strength to do it. In 589 Gao Zhi made a general survey of households and re-registered the people hidden by the great families of the prefectures, so the state's grain revenue and its pool of soldiers grew; equal-field allocation, the grain-and-hemp system and the granaries worked smoothly through the Kaihuang years, the military farms and river transport of Guanzhong, Longyou and the Hexi could move food all the way to Lingzhou, and the fubing levies grew with the expanding body of equal-field peasants. A fourth cause was a choice of method. Turkic cavalry was unbeatable on open grassland, but its strength fell away once it was drawn into the narrow ground between the Hetao and Shuozhou and onto winter pasture; the Sui was prepared to commit three hundred thousand men to a single battle rather than accept a situation in which the Turks came south every year. A fifth cause was the diplomatic cover: the Sui married the imperial clanswoman Princess Anyi to Jieli Qaghan in 599, using the marriage and rich gifts to occupy the attention of the main northern host, while keeping Jieli's son Qimin, already resident inside Sui territory, as a pawn for the internal rising, so that no kahan dared bring every horseman south with him.
impact: 這一仗的直接後果，是草原權力格局的改變與隋朝邊防體制的定型。達頭可汗死後，他與頉利之間的戰爭失去核心，漠北的權力分成了意珍保與頉利兩塊，再加上受隋朝支持的啟民可汗，突厥內部再沒有一個可以服眾的可汗。開皇二十年（600）頉利可汗趁隋朝新喪文帝、政局動搖之際大舉南下，隋朝再發兵出擊，高熲策劃的內應在此顯出作用，頉利大敗，僅以身免；仁壽元年（601），楚王楊諒在靈州一線擒斬達頭之子意珍保，東突厥的分裂局勢至此定型，漠南的游牧政權退到陰山以北。對隋朝本身，這場戰爭帶來兩樣東西。第一樣是防線：同年十二月詔諸州修築長城，在塞內外築城置兵、積粟轉運，河套與陰山南麓從此成為王朝的邊界與屯田地帶，隋朝由「以攻為守」轉為「以守為攻」，直到隋煬帝時才重新轉向進攻。第二樣是代價：達頭部眾十餘萬降隋，加上陸續內附的部眾，國家在邊疆同時背上了安置、給種、編戶與供糧的負擔；開皇末年府兵調發日密，隋朝連續三次大舉征高句麗，耗空了國力，導致民變蜂起、隋室傾覆——隋文帝用兵於北所省下的開支，終究在二十年後從南邊吐了出來。對草原而言，這一場戰爭確立了隋唐時期中原王朝與北方游牧政權互有輸贏的基本格局：中原帝國只要有足夠的兵源與糧道，就能在草原內鬥時取得決定性的戰果；而草原政權若要在內部分裂中勝出，光靠騎兵是不夠的。
impactEn: The immediate consequences were a rearrangement of power on the steppe and the fixing of the Sui frontier system. With Datou dead, the war between him and Jieli lost its pivot, and authority in the north of the steppe split into the hands of Yizhenbao and Jieli, together with the Sui-backed Qimin; there was no longer a kahan whom the steppe could accept. In 600, taking advantage of the Sui's recent mourning for the dead emperor and the confusion that followed, Jieli Qaghan swept south in force; the Sui moved out to meet him, and the internal agent arranged by Gao Zhi now did its work, for Jieli was badly beaten and escaped with nothing but his life. In 601, the first year of Renshou, the Prince of Chu, Yang Liang, captured and beheaded Yizhenbao at Lingzhou, and the fragmented state of the Eastern Turks was thereby settled: the nomadic power withdrew north of the Yin Mountains. The Sui itself gained two things from this war. The first was a frontier. In the twelfth month of the same year the court ordered the prefectures to repair and build the Great Wall, to build forts and station troops inside and outside the frontier and to accumulate grain for transport; the Hetao and the southern foot of the Yin Mountains became the dynasty's border and its farm belt, and the Sui shifted from attacking in defence to holding in defence, not turning back to the offensive until the reign of Yangdi. The second was the cost. More than a hundred thousand of Datou's people came over, and with the tribes that followed, the state took on the burden of settling them, giving them stock, registering them as households and feeding them; as the fubing levies were called out ever more densely near the end of Kaihuang, the Sui spent itself on three great campaigns against Goguryeo, emptied the treasury, and was eaten by rebellion until the dynasty fell: the money saved in the north was paid back with interest in the south twenty years later. For the steppe, the campaign set the basic pattern of the exchanges between the agricultural state and the nomadic powers in the Sui and Tang centuries. An empire with sufficient manpower and a sufficient supply line could take a decisive advantage when the steppe was divided among itself, and a nomadic state trying to survive its own internal war could not do it with cavalry alone.
result: 隋朝在開皇十九年取得了乾淨的勝利。達頭可汗的牙帳被夜襲打散，大軍在追擊中崩潰，他自己被部下所殺，單騎遁走，餘眾十餘萬降隋；靈州與朔州一線的塞外通道被打開，隋朝的追擊一直推進到鐵山、磧口一線，達頭部眾的抵抗意志在缺草、缺水、缺補給的草原上崩解。隋朝隨即在開皇十九年十二月詔諸州修築長城，塞內外築城置兵、積粟轉運，把戰役的成果變成可以長期使用的邊防工程：靈州、朔州一線成為屯田與轉運的基地，降眾被編入州縣、給牛羊令其耕牧，隋朝在漠南第一次擁有了穩定的後方基地。但這一場勝仗並不等於草原平定。頉利可汗仍在漠北稱雄，開皇二十年仍能率眾大舉南下，直到仁壽元年意珍保被擒、啟民可汗成了隋朝在漠南的代理人，東突厥的分裂才告一段落，隋朝邊境又安定了二十餘年，直到隋末天下大亂、突厥再度南下。從兵制與戰爭的觀點看，這場戰役也留下了一套可複用的經驗：以方陣、大盾與長槊硬扛騎兵衝鋒，用弩的齊射把衝鋒打散，再以兩翼騎兵反擊側後；用離間與內應替自己分擔敵人的兵力；最重要的是不靠一場血戰定勝負，而靠把敵人拖到沒有補給的遠處，靠兵源與糧道的持續供應撐到最後。卡面這件羅馬重步兵不在此役現場，但它那句話在靈州到鐵山的四五百公里裡一點都沒錯：戰爭靠的從來不是某一面盾有多厚，而是後面還有多少人、還有多少糧。
resultEn: The Sui won cleanly in the nineteenth year of Kaihuang. The camp of Datou Qaghan was broken by a night attack, the host collapsed during the pursuit, he was killed by his own men, rode out alone, and more than a hundred thousand of his people came over to the Sui. The corridor outside the wall between Lingzhou and Shuozhou was opened, the pursuit ran as far as the Tieshan and Qikou line, and the will to resist broke down in a steppe with no grass, no water and no supply. The Sui then turned the victory into something permanent: in the twelfth month of Kaihuang 19 the prefectures were ordered to build and repair the Great Wall, to build forts and station troops inside and outside the frontier and to accumulate grain for transport, so that the Lingzhou and Shuozhou line became a base for farms and for the transport of supplies, and the surrendered people were enrolled in the prefectures, given cattle and sheep and set to plough and graze. For the first time the Sui held a stable base in the southern steppe. But the victory was not pacification. Jieli Qaghan was still the master in the northern steppe and could still bring a great host south in 600; it was only after Yizhenbao was captured in 601 and Qimin Qaghan had become the Sui's man in the southern steppe that the fragmentation of the Eastern Turks was settled and the frontier enjoyed more than twenty years of quiet, until the collapse of the Sui and the renewed descent of the Turks. From the point of view of military systems and of warfare, the campaign also left behind a set of reusable lessons: meet the cavalry charge with a square, large shields and long spears; break the charge with massed crossbow fire; then send your own cavalry around the flanks. Use division and internal agents to take part of the enemy's strength off him. And above all, do not try to settle the matter in one battle, but drag the enemy out to where he cannot be supplied and hold on with replacements and grain until the end. The Roman legionary on the card was not on that field, but its sentence was exactly right across the four or five hundred kilometres from Lingzhou to Tieshan: what decides a war has never been the thickness of one shield, but how many men and how much grain are still behind you.
